<reflection>
- Run 3 successfully separated the top tier of models, pushing M17 (product-induced deactivation of catS) to the forefront, closely followed by M20, M16, M14, and M7. 
- The low catalyst and high substrate conditions in Run 3 helped distinguish these deactivation models from the rest. However, because Run 3 had no initial product, M17 only differentiated itself later in the reaction as the product accumulated. The NLL gap between M17 and M16/M14 is still only ~1.3 units, meaning the models are still somewhat degenerate.
- The aim for this turn is to definitively break the tie between product-induced deactivation (M17), substrate-induced deactivation (M16), and intrinsic intermediate deactivation (M14).
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To definitively isolate M17 from M16 and M14, we should run an experiment with the maximum allowable initial product (P = 0.5), a low catalyst concentration (cat = 0.01), and a moderate-high substrate concentration (S = 2.5). 
If M17 is the true mechanism, the presence of high initial product will cause immediate, severe deactivation of the catS complex right from t=0, leading to a drastically suppressed initial rate and an extremely early plateau compared to previous runs. 
If M16 is true, the deactivation will depend on the substrate concentration (which is 2.5, half of Run 3), so it will deactivate slower than in Run 3 and be completely unaffected by the initial product. 
If M14 is true, deactivation depends only on the concentration of catS, which will be saturated, leading to a constant deactivation rate regardless of S or P. 
Furthermore, the very low catalyst concentration (0.01) will heavily suppress any second-order catalyst deactivation mechanisms (M18, M19), ensuring they do not confound the results. This targeted condition will force a massive divergence in the predicted kinetic curves of the top 5 models.
</hypothesis>
